'''Márcio Vieira de Vasconcelos''' (born 10 October 1984), known as '''Vieira''', is an Andorran [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[midfielder]].

==Club career==
Born in [[Andorra la Vella]] to [[Portuguese people|Portuguese parents]] who hailed from [[Marco de Canaveses]], [[Porto District]],<ref name=TS>{{cite web|url=https://www.tamegasousa.pt/marco-andorra-convoca-jogador-com-descendencia-marcuense-para-defrontar-portugal/|title=MARCO: Andorra convoca jogador com ascendência marcuense para defrontar Portugal|trans-title=MARCO: Andorra call player of ''marcuense'' descent to play Portugal|publisher=Tâmega Sousa|first=Miguel|last=Ângelo|language=pt|date=7 October 2016|access-date=22 March 2018|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210527063335/https://www.tamegasousa.pt/marco-andorra-convoca-jogador-com-descendencia-marcuense-para-defrontar-portugal/|archive-date=27 May 2021}}</ref> Vieira's biggest achievement as a professional was appearing for [[F.C. Marco]] in two [[Liga Portugal 2|Segunda Liga]] seasons even though he only played a total of 15 matches, all in [[2005–06 Liga de Honra|2005–06]].<ref name=TS/> He all but spent the rest of his career in [[Football in Spain|Spanish amateur football]], his first team being [[UD Ibiza-Eivissa|SE Eivissa-Ibiza]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.heraldo.es/aficion/noticias/marcio-vieira-jugar-barbastro-jugar-ronaldo/|title=Marcio Vieira igual juega contra el Barbastro que contra la Portugal de Ronaldo|trans-title=Marcio Vieira takes on Barbastro as he does Ronaldo's Portugal|newspaper=[[Heraldo de Aragón]]|language=es|date=10 October 2016|access-date=22 March 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.heraldo.es/noticias/aficion/2017/02/23/real-zaragoza-atletico-monzon-fraga-reciben-dinero-la-uefa.html|title=El Real Zaragoza, el Atlético de Monzón y el Fraga reciben dinero de la UEFA|trans-title=Real Zaragoza, Atlético de Monzón and Fraga take money from UEFA|newspaper=Heraldo de Aragón|first=Emilio|last=Ralla|language=es|date=23 February 2017|access-date=26 March 2021|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190327135938/https://www.heraldo.es/noticias/aficion/2017/02/23/real-zaragoza-atletico-monzon-fraga-reciben-dinero-la-uefa.html|archive-date=27 March 2019}}</ref>

Vieira signed for [[Atlético Monzón]] in summer 2008, remaining in [[Aragon]] for 15 years.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.rtp.pt/noticias/futebol-internacional/marcio-vieira-chegou100a-internacionalizacao-por-andorra_d1276568|title=Márcio Vieira {{sic|nolink=y|chegou100.ª}} internacionalização por Andorra|trans-title=Márcio Vieira reached 100th cap for Andorra|publisher=[[Rádio e Televisão de Portugal]]|language=pt|date=19 November 2020|access-date=28 March 2023|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230418072843/https://www.rtp.pt/noticias/futebol-internacional/marcio-vieira-chegou100a-internacionalizacao-por-andorra_d1276568|archive-date=18 April 2023}}</ref><ref name=Elite>{{cite news|url=https://www.heraldo.es/noticias/deportes/futbol/2021/03/25/marcio-vieira-de-tercera-division-a-codearse-con-la-elite-mundial-1480334.html|title=Marcio Vieira, de Tercera División a codearse con la élite mundial|trans-title=Marcio Vieira, from ''Tercera División'' to going head to head against the world's elite|newspaper=Heraldo de Aragón|first=Emilio|last=Ralla|language=es|date=25 March 2021|access-date=28 March 2023|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230328210432/https://www.heraldo.es/noticias/deportes/futbol/2021/03/25/marcio-vieira-de-tercera-division-a-codearse-con-la-elite-mundial-1480334.html|archive-date=28 March 2023}}</ref> The 38-year-old returned to Portugal on 27 July 2023, joining amateurs [[A.D. Marco 09]] who had [[Phoenix club (sports)|risen from the ashes]] of his first club.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.tamegasousa.pt/internacional-andorrano-marcio-vieira-e-reforco-do-marco-09/|title=Internacional andorrano Márcio Vieira é reforço do Marco-09|trans-title=Andorran international Márcio Vieira is addition to Marco-09|publisher=Tâmega Sousa|first=Luís|last=Nogueira|language=pt|date=27 July 2023|access-date=4 August 2023|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230804131623/https://www.tamegasousa.pt/internacional-andorrano-marcio-vieira-e-reforco-do-marco-09/|archive-date=4 August 2023}}</ref>

==International career==
Vieira won his first [[Cap (sport)|cap]] for the [[Andorra national football team|Andorra national team]] on 12 October 2005, starting and being [[Substitute (association football)|replaced]] early into the second half of a 0–3 home loss against [[Armenia national football team|Armenia]] for the [[2006 FIFA World Cup]] [[2006 FIFA World Cup qualification (UEFA)|qualifiers]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://espndeportes-assets.espn.com/futbol/cronica?id=178874|title=Pasó sin pena ni gloria|trans-title=As unassuming as can be|publisher=[[ESPN Deportes]]|language=es|date=12 October 2005|access-date=22 March 2018|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180909035611/http://espndeportes-assets.espn.go.com/futbol/cronica?id=178874|archive-date=9 September 2018}}</ref><ref name=TS/> He played his 100th international on 17 November 2020, in the 5–0 defeat to [[Latvia national football team|Latvia]] for the [[2020–21 UEFA Nations League]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.rtp.pt/noticias/futebol-internacional/marcio-vieira-chegou100a-internacionalizacao-por-andorra_d1276568|title=Márcio Vieira chegou 100.ª internacionalização por Andorra|trans-title=Márcio Vieira reached 100th cap for Andorra|publisher=[[Rádio e Televisão de Portugal]]|language=pt|date=19 November 2020|access-date=26 March 2021|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201126155014/https://www.rtp.pt/noticias/futebol-internacional/marcio-vieira-chegou100a-internacionalizacao-por-andorra_d1276568|archive-date=26 November 2020}}</ref>
